description: Granularity-explicit, adjudicated judge. Every acceptable entry carries granularity: "symbol" (a symbolRegex is set and must match) or "path" (a whole-file result on a matching path is accepted). Built from the 54 entries of conceptual-cases.json, minus every entry the blind adjudicator judged `no`, with every remaining symbolRegex:null entry either replaced by a symbol-level entry or explicitly marked path-level.
portabilityNote: Unlike judge-v1 this judge is not bound to one index state: it is expressed as path/symbol regexes, so it can be re-applied to any log that carries a result.json with per-hit path, symbol and granularity. It IS bound to the pinned source commits recorded in `repos` below.
scoring: rank = position (1-based) of the first top-10 result whose path matches an acceptable pathRegex and whose symbol name matches symbolRegex (or symbolRegex is null, or the result is a whole-file result on a matching path). strictRank additionally requires a symbol-level result when symbolRegex is set. Variants: original, rewritten, fresh. Splits: tune (react, polars), heldout (flatbuffers). Cohorts: gap, control.
strictVsLenient: STRICT counts only entries with granularity "symbol": a hit needs a symbol-level result whose symbol matches that entry's symbolRegex. LENIENT counts symbol-level and path-level entries, so a whole-file result on a path-level entry's path also scores. The two columns diverge exactly on queries that have at least one path-level entry. Under judge-v1 the two columns are identical by construction, because chunk IDs carry no granularity.
denominatorRule: Hit@k and MRR divide by every query in the log, unanswerable ones included, matching what the historical v1-era scorecard did. The unanswerable count is printed in its own column so the fair-test denominator (n - unanswerable) is one subtraction away and nothing is silently dropped or silently absorbed into a miss.

Its totals: 54 entries -> 24 yes / 10 no / 20 path-only, 6 pathRegexes matching zero files, 8 path-only entries needing narrowing. See v2-adjudication.md "Blinding attestation".

derivedFrom.rule: A REMOVE verdict is applied literally: the entry is dropped and no replacement regex is substituted for it. A query left with zero entries is marked unanswerable:true rather than deleted, so it is excluded from the strict/lenient denominators instead of silently counting as a retrieval miss. NARROW verdicts ARE applied, because step 2 of the brief asks for exactly that replacement, and the adjudicator supplied the replacement regex.
